column1: # Opening-hours oracle for 500 Lviv OSM values, generated once and committed (T-0209).
# Query: pyosmium 4.3.2; every node and way carrying an `opening_hours` tag with a node
#        inside lat 49.72..49.95, lon 23.85..24.15 (Lviv) - 4881 places, 1309 distinct values.
# Selection: all distinct values that use PH/SH, off/closed, a quoted comment, a weekday
#        index, a month/date range, or an open-ended `+` time (86 values) excluding the one
#        named below, then the most frequent remaining distinct values, to 500.
# Excluded, not dropped silently: `Mo-Su 08:00-18:00,08:00-18:00+` is a duplicate range with
#        a stray trailing `+`. opening_hours.js reports an inconsistent unknown 00:00-04:00
#        window for it, so it is not a usable oracle; the evaluator reads it as the same
#        08:00-18:00 range twice. This is the only candidate value excluded.
# Oracle: npm opening_hours@3.15.0 (LGPL-3.0, used only to generate this file), Node v24.18.0,
#        TZ=Europe/Kyiv, nominatim anchor {lat 49.8419, lon 24.0316, country_code ua, state Lviv}.
# Instants: ten fixed UTC instants covering a public holiday, a weekday, a weekend, both
#        2026 DST transitions and a midnight crossing.
# Columns: osm_type, osm_id, lat, lon, opening_hours, instant_utc, expected_state
# expected_state is open, closed or unknown, and is what opening_hours.js reports for that
# raw value at that instant on the Europe/Kyiv wall clock.
